zone_metadata.description: Master the fundamentals: OSI Model, protocols, media types, and network architectures.

nodes.name: The Seven Layers
nodes.objective: 1.1 - Explain concepts related to the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) reference model

encounters.question: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for routing packets between different networks?
encounters.explanation: Layer 3 (Network) handles logical addressing and routing using IP addresses. Layer 2 uses MAC addresses for local delivery, Layer 4 manages TCP/UDP connections, and Layer 7 is the application interface.

encounters.question: At which OSI layer do hubs operate?
encounters.explanation: Hubs operate at Layer 1 (Physical). They simply repeat electrical signals to all ports without any intelligence. Switches operate at Layer 2, routers at Layer 3.

encounters.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for establishing, maintaining, and terminating sessions between applications?
encounters.explanation: Layer 5 (Session) manages sessions. Layer 4 (Transport) handles TCP/UDP, Layer 6 handles encryption/encoding, and Layer 7 is the application itself.

encounters.question: Which OSI layer handles data compression and encryption?
encounters.explanation: Layer 6 (Presentation) handles data formatting, compression, and encryption (like SSL/TLS). It's the 'translator' between application and network formats.

nodes.name: The Toolbox
nodes.objective: 1.2 - Compare and contrast networking appliances, applications, and functions

encounters.question: Which device makes forwarding decisions based on IP addresses?
encounters.explanation: Routers operate at Layer 3 and use IP addresses to route packets between networks. Switches use MAC addresses (Layer 2), hubs are Layer 1.

encounters.question: What is the primary purpose of a load balancer?
options: To distribute traffic across multiple servers
encounters.explanation: Load balancers distribute incoming network/application traffic across multiple servers to prevent any single server from becoming a bottleneck.

encounters.question: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?
options: IDS blocks traffic, IPS only logs
IDS detects threats, IPS detects AND blocks threats
IDS is hardware, IPS is software
encounters.explanation: IDS (Intrusion Detection System) alerts on suspicious activity. IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) detects and automatically takes action to block threats.

nodes.name: The Secret Codes
nodes.objective: 1.4 - Explain common networking ports, protocols, services, and traffic types

encounters.question: Which port does HTTP use by default?
encounters.explanation: HTTP uses port 80. Port 21 is FTP, 25 is SMTP, and 443 is HTTPS.

encounters.question: Which protocol uses port 22?
encounters.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) uses port 22 for encrypted remote access. SFTP also uses port 22. Telnet (unencrypted) uses port 23.

encounters.question: What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?
options: TCP is connection-oriented, UDP is connectionless
UDP is more secure than TCP
TCP only works on wireless networks
encounters.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented with guaranteed delivery, acknowledgments, and error checking. UDP is connectionless - it sends packets without waiting for confirmation, making it faster but less reliable.

encounters.question: Which port range defines 'well-known ports'?
encounters.explanation: Well-known ports are 0-1023 (assigned by IANA for standard services). Registered ports are 1024-49151. Dynamic/private ports are 49152-65535.

guardian_exam.name: The OSI Overlord
guardian_exam.description: You face the towering construct of the 7 layers. Only those who truly understand network fundamentals may pass.

questions.question: Which device operates at Layer 2 of the OSI model?
questions.explanation: Switches operate at Layer 2 using MAC addresses.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a proxy server?
options: Act as an intermediary between clients and servers
questions.explanation: Proxy servers act as intermediaries, enhancing security and privacy.

questions.question: Which port does DNS use?
questions.explanation: DNS uses port 53 (both TCP and UDP).
